cards.text: Jesus arrives in Bethany, where Lazarus, the brother of Martha and Mary, has died. Bethany is a little less than two miles from Jerusalem, and many people have come to comfort the two sisters. Friend, that house is FULL.

cards.question: When Jesus arrives, Lazarus has already spent ___ days in the tomb.

cards.text: Then word reaches the house. Jesus is coming.

cards.question: When they hear Jesus is coming, Martha and Mary both go out together to meet Him.

cards.text: Martha goes out to meet Him, but Mary stays at home. Martha gets right to it: “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”

cards.question: But Martha isn't finished. Even now, what does Martha say she knows?

answers.text: God will give Jesus whatever He asks
Lazarus is resting at peace with God
Jesus came as fast as He could

cards.text: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus tells her. Short and simple.

cards.question: Martha says she already knows Lazarus will rise again. When does she say it will happen?

answers.text: In the resurrection at the last day
Three days after he was buried
Once the time of mourning is over

cards.text: Martha is thinking about the last day. Then Jesus says, “I am the resurrection and the life.”

cards.question: Jesus tells Martha that whoever believes in Him will live, even though he dies.

cards.text: Jesus adds that everyone who lives and believes in Him will never die. Then He asks her straight out: “Do you believe this?”

cards.question: Jesus asks Martha if she believes this. What does Martha say she believes about Jesus?

answers.text: That He is the Christ the Son of God
That He is a great prophet from Galilee
That He is a wise teacher from Nazareth

cards.text: After that, Martha goes back and calls Mary aside: “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”

cards.question: When Mary hears the Teacher is asking for her, she gets up ___ and goes to Him.

cards.text: Jesus is still out where Martha met Him, and when the people comforting Mary see her rush out, they ALL follow. Like when one coworker stands up fast and the whole office stands up with her, not even sure why.

cards.question: Where do the people following Mary suppose she is going?

cards.text: Mary reaches Jesus. She sees Him and falls at His feet.

cards.question: When Mary reaches Jesus, she says the exact same words Martha said when she met Him.

cards.text: Jesus sees Mary weeping, and the people who came with her weeping too. He is deeply moved in spirit and troubled.

cards.question: Seeing Mary and the others weeping, Jesus asks them a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: Who was with him at the end

cards.question: Then come just two words: Jesus ___.

cards.text: Some of the people watching say, “See how He loved him!”

cards.question: Others ask whether the man who opened the eyes of the blind could have kept Lazarus from dying.

cards.text: Jesus, deeply moved once again, comes to the tomb.

cards.question: What kind of tomb is Lazarus in?

answers.text: A cave with a stone across the entrance
A pit dug deep into the ground
A room carved out under the house

cards.text: “Take away the stone,” Jesus says. And Martha, the dead man's sister, speaks right up.

cards.question: Jesus wants the stone taken away from Lazarus's tomb. What is Martha worried about?

answers.text: After four days he will stink
The stone is too heavy to move
The crowd will be too upset

cards.text: “Lord, by now he stinks,” Martha says. Friend, I've been sugarcoating cookies for years, and Martha just will NOT sugarcoat anything.

cards.question: Jesus answers Martha by reminding her that He told her if she believed, she would see the glory of God.

cards.text: So they take away the stone. Jesus lifts His eyes upward and says, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.”

cards.question: Jesus says He knew the Father always hears Him. So why does He thank the Father out loud?

answers.text: So the people will believe the Father sent Him
So the disciples will learn how to pray
So Martha will stop being afraid

cards.text: After He says this, Jesus calls out in a LOUD voice. Friend, I spent years in the dark of a junk drawer, waiting for somebody to call my name.

cards.question: Standing at the open tomb, what does Jesus call out in a loud voice?
The man who had been dead comes out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen and his face wrapped in a cloth.
Lazarus is standing there all bound up, and Jesus tells them, “___ him and let him go.”

cards.text: We're stopping right here, friend. Trust me, this story is still in the oven.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 18 quotes "___ him and let him go.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "That He is a wise teacher from Nazareth" is not false in the passage. Martha calls Jesus "The Teacher" in John 11:28, so a baker could argue this answer describes what Martha believes about Him.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The joke says the people follow Mary "not even sure why." John 11:31 says they followed her supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn, and card 16 then asks what they supposed. The comparison doesn't share the passage's action and works against the next question.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question, but the wrong answer "A room carved out under the house" is not a real detail from anywhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question says "What is Martha worried about?" This states a feeling as fact. John 11:39 gives only Martha's words, not a feeling.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The right answer "After four days he will stink" puts the smell in the future. In John 11:39 Martha says "by now he stinks," which is already the case.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This card repeats what card 10 just answered: Martha's objection about the smell in John 11:39. It recaps instead of moving the passage forward. The joke could go on card 9 or card 13 instead.

The wrong answers "Lazarus wake up now" and "Lazarus arise and walk" mean nearly the same as "Lazarus come out." Each is a call for the dead man to get up and come, so a baker could argue for either one.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Lazarus arise and walk" sounds older and more like the Bible than the other two answers, so the answers don't sound alike.

rule.text: None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain retelling with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Examples are stop 1 cards 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 17, and stop 2 cards 1, 3, 5, 7 and 13. The passage has room for voice that fits its grief, like his reactions, disbelief and storyteller lines, but only stop 1 card 1, stop 1 card 15 and stop 2 card 11 try it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Five of the six true or false cards are True, and all three in stop 2 are True (cards 6, 12 and 17). Several are close retellings of the verse, like stop 2 card 17, so they read as obviously true and can be answered without reasoning. Stop 2 card 17 also gives Lazarus coming out of the tomb, the passage's climax, only inside a true or false statement.
findings.question: Should the docs require a mix of True and False answers across true or false cards? Should they also say that a statement retelling the verse closely enough to be obviously true doesn't meet the informed-guess rule?
